title: Graphic texts: understanding the clear (overt) message
canonical_examples_source: Language rules self-verified; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024-gps (KS2 GPS).

blocks.content: Posters, signs and adverts are graphic texts — they mix words with pictures. Some of their message is stated clearly and directly. That is the overt message. Quick words: graphic text means a message using both words and pictures together to share information.
An overt message is the clear, directly stated message of a graphic text.

steps: A poster shows a rubbish bin and the words 'Keep our park clean'.
The stated message is: do not litter — keep the park clean.

blocks.question: A road sign shows a red circle and the words 'No Entry'. What is the overt message?
options: do not go in this way
blocks.explain: The sign states it directly: do not enter this way.
blocks.rule: An overt message is the clear, directly stated message of a graphic text.

practiceItems.prompt: a message stated clearly and directly is ___ (overt/hidden)
an overt message is easy to ___ (read/miss)
a text that mixes words and pictures is a ___ text

blocks.content: To find the overt message, read the words and look at the main picture together.

blocks.question: A poster shows a toothbrush and says 'Brush twice a day'. The overt message is:
options: brush your teeth twice every day
blocks.explain: The words state it plainly: brush your teeth twice a day.
blocks.rule: Read the words and the main image together to find the overt message.

practiceItems.prompt: the clear stated message of a poster is the ___ message
read the words and the ___ together
a poster mixing words and images is a ___ text

blocks.question: A poster shows a big apple and the words 'Eat fruit every day!' What is the overt (clearly stated) message?
options: Eat fruit every day — it is stated plainly in words
blocks.explain: An overt message is the one stated plainly. This poster spells it out in words: 'Eat fruit every day.' You do not need to dig for it — it is right there.
blocks.rule: The overt message is the one stated plainly in the text or words.
blocks.principle: Media texts carry clear (overt) messages you can read directly.
canonical_solution: The poster's words say 'Eat fruit every day'
So it is the overt message

rubric.look_for: reads the plain words on the poster

misconceptions.coach: The overt message is the one written plainly.
The words 'Eat fruit every day' are the message.
